text.p: These are the stories making headlines in the Namibian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Namibia stands to lose more than N$ 110 million in revenue under the current Southern African Customs Union if South Africa alone signs a free trade pact with the European Union. In a report commissioned by the European Development Fund to assess the impact of the proposed EU-SA free trade agreement on other SACU members, Harare-based consultancy Imani Development says Namibia's grain milling, meat, fish and beer products would be hardest hit.

- Chief of the Kxoe community, Kippie George, has briefed the United Nations about government's plans to evict his tribe from their tourism sites in the West Caprivi. He was addressing the 15th session of the UN working group on indigenous populations in Geneva.

- "We have lost faith in the Namibian government, because it only pays lipservice to minority rights", Kxoe San chief Kippie George told 700 delegates at the 15th session of the UN working group on indigenous populations in Geneva at the beginning of this month.

- The economic integration into the SADC region could seriously affect the competitiveness of the Namibian dairy industry, Bernd Rothkegel, director of planning in the Ministry of Agriculture, told dairy farmers in Hardap on Wednesday.

- A child-smuggling network, the paedophile Gert van Rooyen and Windhoek are being brought into connection with each other, following the disappearance of yet another South African schoolgirl six months ago. The South African police now fears that the suicide of van Rooyen and his girlfriend Joey Haarhoff has not brought the end of the spate of kidnappings of under-age girls.

- Namibia may be hosting two major conferences within the next four years, which will bring 12,000 to 14,000 delegates to this country. One is the next World Youth Festival in 2001, while the other is the International Parliamentary Forum in April next year.
